floor_history.headline: Floor 12->9 (pure C); honest floor is a 4-reg rotation reduced to a single-register sub-problem: copy_end must land in callee-saved s5.

Floor holds 9. Instrumented cc1 PROVES copy_end->s5 is unreachable via allocno priority (livelen capped ~38 << const's locked 76; find_reg has no cost/preference lever); def/use-placement axis exhaust

frontier.hypothesis: G1: a C form whose pre-alloc (post-sched1) RTL gives copy_end a longer, or const a shorter, live length while sched2/reorg restores the identical emitted bytes.
frontier.mechanism: reg_live_length is measured after cse/loop/flow/combine/sched1 but before reload; two sources emitting the same final bytes can present different pre-alloc livelens.
frontier.next_probe: Diff cc1 -da .sched1/.combine dumps of candidate vs an m2c-reconstructed target C to see whether the do-loop's copy_end-use can sit later in pre-alloc RTL without moving the emitted loop.

frontier.hypothesis: G2: induce a legitimate hard_reg_copy_preference that pulls copy_end to s5 (bypassing priority), without a register pin.
frontier.mechanism: find_reg (global.c:1046+) overrides best_reg to a preferred reg when a copy insn links the allocno to that reg; copy_end currently has none.
frontier.next_probe: Explore expressing the loop end-pointer as a copy from another pointer variable (byte-neutral) that would create a copy-preference; verify via ALLOCDBG + sandbox.

frontier.hypothesis: G3: re-derive the s5 identity — confirm the original loop bound is a src-relative end pointer and not a down-counter / dest-relative form that changes which value is long-lived.
frontier.mechanism: m2c reconstruction + coalescing/aliasing check may reveal a different allocno set where the long-lived value naturally takes s4 and the short one s5.
frontier.next_probe: Run m2c on the target and inspect the loop shape and any reg_may_share coalescing against the candidate.
